newsitem.title: SUDAN: U.S. embassy in Sudan hails peace agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. embassy in Sudan hails peace agreement.

text.p: The U.S. embassy in Khartoum on Wednesday welcomed the signing of a peace agreement between the Sudanese government and southern rebel factions earlier this month but it urged further talks with other rebels.

The main rebel group the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang refused to sign the agreement on April 21, saying the government of Lieutenant General Omar Hassan al-Bashir was not serious about peace.

The embassy said in a press release that the agreement has set important precedents that address the concerns of southerners. "They promise to figure in the search for a complete and lasting peace among all the parties in the civil war," it added.

"We believe that the ideas in both the peace agreement and the (Intergovernmental Authority on Development) IGAD declaration of principles form a solid basis on which to draw this tragic conflict to a peaceful conclusion. We urge the government of Sudan to seek peaceful negotiations with the factions still fighting," the statement said.
IGAD, which comprises Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan and Uganda, aims to help settle conflicts in the region, in addition to its main mission of boosting development.
